turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. My son found out he had a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, Hale, and on what basis?
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I know your schedule is brutal.
Don't manage my schedule, Hale. You asked for this meeting, so tell me what you have against Owen's essay.
I have to say, you're far more reasonable than I expected. Most parents come in swinging.
Save it. You've used two of my twenty minutes and haven't shown me one thing. What do you have?
It's refreshing. You clearly see the whole picture, so I think we're really on the same side here.
Then why is there a zero in the gradebook? I'm not on your side, Hale; I'm on Owen's. Show me your evidence, or I'm going to the principal's office when we're done.
